newsitem.title: UK: U.S. stocks in London down, techs extend losses.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks in London down, techs extend losses.

text.p: U.S. stocks weakened in London trading on Monday, dragged lower by further profit taking in the technology sector, dealers said.
The Dow was expected to open some 20 points lower, extending the heavy losses suffered on Friday when the index fell 130.31 points to close at 7,890.46.
Shares in semiconductor company Intel Corp traded down $1-5/16 at $85-1/8 as investors took profits after recent sharp gains in the stock.
"After some monumental rises in the tech stocks, people are not afraid to lock in some profits," said one dealer.
Shares in International Business Machines Corp, which was due to report second quarter earnings after the market closes on Monday, were quoted down $3/4 at $103-1/2.

Dealers said in the absence of significant economic data due this week, investors would focus on Fed chairman Alan Greenspan's semi-annual testimony to the House Banking Subcommittee on Tuesday and his appearance before the Senate banking Committee on Wednesday.
However, dealers said Greenspan was not expected to deliver any shocks regarding interest rates since recent economic indicators suggested inflation pressures remained under control.
Recent Wall Street volatility has sparked some fears that a sharp market correction could be in the offing.
A report in the U.S. investment newspaper Barron's for example drew parallels between Wall Street's recent performance and before previous crashes in 1929 and 1987.
Yet dealers here played down the importance such market anxieties, pointing out that the backdrop of low inflation and interest rates remained in place.
"The markets may be a bit overvalued," said one head of sales at a U.S. investment bank here, "but some people were saying that six months ago and it hasn't done them much good."
